outcome.technical: (1) _clause_coverage.py: the reader's choices are one table, READING_CHOICES (choice, strict, wide): fold (False | True: NFKC with format characters dropped, `_fold`), marker (_MARK_EXACT, the exact `Acceptance:` | _MARK_ANY, the word in any case with following emphasis/blanks/colon taken into the marker), opener (_LINE_OPENER `[ \t#>*_+-]*` | _ANY_LINE_OPENER, the same plus a backtick), colonAnywhere (False | True), forms ((_PAREN_FORM, _LINE_FORM) tried alone, earliest read | (_ANY_FORM,): `(n)`, `n.`, `n)`, `[n]` at a line start after an indent and a bullet, mixed, or `(n)` after a blank). STRICT and WIDE are the two columns; `_read(text, choices)` is the one reader both go through (markers, bodies, `_read_body`, choice of marker), and `_opens(body, offset, layout, marker_indent, form)` replaces `_paren_opens`/`_line_opens` with per-form parameters bind/restart/nest (strict paren: F/F/F, strict line: T/T/F, wide: F/T/T - nest reads a 1 written another way than the list's last opener as a nested list, so sub-steps stay quiet). A marker away from a line's start must hold its colon in both columns (every strict match ends in one, so strict is unchanged). acceptance_reading(description, wide=True) reads strict, then `_wide_reading` compares: same count and each item equal once both are folded, else `wide` = {count, line, text} with the first line where the per-line item maps differ, quoted as written; acceptance_items passes wide=False so task_clauses does not pay for it. The line adds `a wider reading of the same text finds N items, and the two readings first part on line L: "..."` as the first departure. `_tail` cuts at _TAKE (= _QUOTE_WIDTH * 4) where it is taken, and finds the line end only inside that window.
